items.title: Make the pre-boot download progress legible and informative
items.what: Pre-boot loading screen (ShoeMoney logo): the progress bar is a 1–2px-tall line near the very bottom edge with very low contrast against the dark background, and there’s no numeric progress (no %/MB), so it reads like a decorative divider rather than progress.
items.why: In the first 5 seconds, players judge whether the game is working; an unreadable progress indicator increases bounce and “stuck loading” reports.
items.how: Increase bar height to ~6–8px, raise contrast (lighter fill + darker track), and add a compact label above it (e.g., “Downloading… 42%” or “12/28 MB”) centered; also move the bar up by ~24–32px to avoid bottom-edge/gesture-area ambiguity.

items.title: Hide/disable the twin-stick controls during the QUALIFIER intro/countdown
items.what: QUALIFIER intro screen (with big “FIGHT” button): both large virtual sticks are already visible and look active under the CTA, while the UI also says “STARTING IN 2/3/4”; this creates three competing focal points (title card, Fight button, sticks) in the lower half.
items.why: It’s unclear what the player should do (tap FIGHT vs. start moving sticks), which is costly on first-match comprehension for a touch-first game.
items.how: Stage the UI: during intro/countdown, either (a) hide the sticks entirely and show a single CTA (Tap to start / Fight), or (b) show the sticks at reduced opacity with a “Locked” state and no thumb indicators; fade them in and enable input only when the round actually begins.

items.title: Fix half-point score rendering so it can’t read as “21/2”
items.what: Results screen (“HASANABI WINS”): the top-right score shows a half point as a stacked “2 1/2” style string (visually reads like “21/2”) rather than an unambiguous “2.5” or true “2½” glyph.
items.why: Point-karate scoring is already nonstandard for many players; ambiguous typography makes the win condition feel confusing/untrustworthy.
items.how: Standardize on one format everywhere: either render halves as decimal (2.5) or use a single-character fraction glyph (½) from a font that supports it; if using a glyph, include it in the UI font subset and render as one token (no slash layout).

items.title: Add contact shadows to anchor the photoreal fighters to the tatami
items.what: In-fight screens (dojo background): both fighters’ feet look like they’re sitting on top of the mat texture with little/no localized darkening under soles; the lack of a tight contact shadow makes them read as cutouts floating over the floor.
items.why: This breaks the ‘premium’ look immediately (mixed 3D + photoreal sprites) and reduces depth/impact when strikes land because characters don’t feel physically placed in the scene.
items.how: Add a shadow-catcher pass under each fighter: a soft blob/contact shadow (elliptical, blurred) that scales/offsets with stance and foot positions; if you have per-fighter depth, use a simple projected shadow quad; otherwise, attach 1–2 blobs to each ankle/foot bone and blend multiply at ~20–35% opacity.

items.title: Increase readability of the stance/technique hint strip and directional cues
items.what: In-fight HUD (above the sticks): the “STANCE / TECHNIQUE” hint strip uses very small text and thin arrow glyphs; on the 390px-wide portrait shots it’s hard to parse at a glance, and the tiny left/right/up/down markers compete with the similarly subtle chevrons around the sticks.
items.why: Players can’t quickly learn the control language, leading to random swipes/inputs and early churn—especially critical in the first round.
items.how: Bump hint-strip font size and weight (e.g., +2–3px and semibold), increase contrast (lighter text or darker pill), and replace tiny triangle glyphs with the same iconography used on the sticks (matching arrow/chevron shapes); optionally show only the last input + next expected input instead of the full list to reduce density.
